METHODS OF CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF FERROSILICON
PART II DETERMINATION OF CARBON

( First Revision )
0. FO,REWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29January 1982, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 IS : 1559-1961* which covers chemical analysis of different ferroalloys, namely, ferrosilicon, ferrochromimn, ferromanganese and speigeleisen, silicomanganese, ferromolvbdenum, ferrophosphorus, ferrotitanium, ferrovanadium and ferrotungsten, was first published in 1961. While reviewing this standard, the Sectional -Committee felt that the standard should be revised to cover ferrosilicon, and methods of analysis of other ferl-o-alloys should be covered in separate standards. During preparation of the revision of IS : 1559-l961* it was felt convenient to cover methods of chemical analysis of ferrosilicon in different parts of the standard which on publication would supersede Section I ferrosilicon The committee also decided to rewrite the methods of IS : 1559-1961*.' taking into consideration the latest composition specified in IS : 11 lo19817. Though calcium and manganese are not specified in IS : 11 lol981t, the determination of these elements are covered in this standard because these are generally required from the view point of determining intereference of analysis in methods for determining other elements in ferrosilicon due to presence of these elements. Moreover the determination of these `elements may be required for comprehensive analysis This part covers the determination of carbon. The other of ferrosilicon. parts cover as follows: Part I Part III __ .._. Determination Determination of silicon of sulphur

0.3 In this part only direct combustion gravimetric method has been retained and the reference of relevant Jndian Standard for the apparatus to be used has been given. 0.4 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. _

4. DETERMINATION OF CARBON ( TOTAL) COMBUSTION GRAVIMETRIC METHOD

BY THE DIRECT

4.1 Outline of the Method - The sample is burnt in a stream of pure oxygen, and the resulting I carbon dioxide is absorbed in soda asbestos after removal of the contaminants. From the increase in weight ofthe absorbent the carbon content is calculated. 4.2 Apparatui i The 19715 may be used. apparatus recommended in IS : 6226 ( Part. I )-

4.4 Procedure 4.4.1 Heat the furnace to a temperature between 1 250 and 1 35OY.L Before starting the analysis, test the apparatus for any leaks. Pass a slow stream of oxygen for about 15 minutes through the whole train of the apparatus and then weigh the carbon dioxide absorption tube. A counterpoise of a similar bottle is recommended in a balance. fix weighing. After taking, the first weight connect it back to the apparatus, pass oxygen for 15 minutes and weigh again. If constant mass is obtained, the apparatus is ready for use. Cl.2 Weigh 2.0 g of the sample mixed with 2.0 g of a low carbon standard steel of known carbon content and place in a previously ignited combustion boat made of either porcelain, refractory, clay, nickel-she& or alumina and of dimensions about 100 x 20 x 15 mm with wall as thin as possible and cover the sample with lead foil ( I.5 g twice folded ). Before placing the sample in the boat sprinkie in the bottom of- the boat some burnt magnesite brick dust which has been tested by the blank run ( SGP 44.3 ). Insert the boat quickly into the hot xone of the furnace, with the rubber stopper replaced at the end of the combustion tube, wait for about a minute so that the boat attains the temperature of the furnace and pass a rapid stream ( 300 to 500 ml Per minute ) of oxygen At the end of this for 10 to 15 fninutes to sweep out carbon dioxide. period, remove the carbon dioxide absorption bulb, cool in a desiccator The and weigh quickly against a. similar tube used as a counterpoise. increase in mass represents carbon dioxide. 4.63 Carry out a blank determination on 2-O g of the same low carbon standard steel that was mixed with the sample.' 45 Caledation Carbon, percent = where ( k -
